football-match.text: Football has had an offside law since the Football Association’s first written rules in 1863.
The assistant referee signals offside by raising the flag; the referee then decides whether to stop play.
A player cannot be offside in their own half, or directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick.
After an offside, the defending team restarts with an indirect free kick from where the offence happened.
Level counts as onside: being level with the second-last opponent is not an offence.

the-missing-crown.text: A coronation is the ceremony in which a monarch is formally crowned.
A chancellor is traditionally a monarch’s senior official and adviser.
Torn threads and fibres are classic clues in mystery stories, because they can tie a person to a place.
In royal households, a captain of the guard was responsible for protecting the monarch and the crown jewels.
This film’s captions are timed to its narration, so Selene only uses lines you have already heard.
